title: Payment and Settlement Systems (Finality and Netting) (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Payment and Settlement Systems (Finality and Netting) (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: Designated payment and settlement systems
sections.summary: Five payment and settlement systems have been designated, including CLS, MEPS+, SGD and USD cheque clearing, and GIRO.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Five payment and settlement systems have been designated so far: (a) the Continuous Linked Settlement System (CLS) – the international foreign exchange settlement system; (b) the New MAS Electronic Payment System (MEPS+) – our nation’s sole large value Singapore Dollar real-time gross settlement system used by banks and financial institutions; (c) the Singapore Dollar (SGD) Cheque Clearing System; (d) the United States Dollar (USD) Cheque Clearing and Settlement System; and (e) the General Interbank Recurring Order (GIRO) System.

sections.label: Aims of the Bill
sections.summary: The Bill aims to enhance payment transaction protection, set designation criteria for MAS, and strengthen MAS' administrative powers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Taking these developments into account, the Bill aims to achieve the following: (a) enhance the protection of payment transactions by extending the period during which transactions enjoy finality and, hence, protect a wider range of transactions from insolvency law in a liquidation event; (b) set out clear criteria for MAS to designate such systems; and (c) strengthen MAS’ administrative powers.

sections.label: Extending insolvency protection
sections.summary: The Bill amends insolvency protection of transfer orders, netting and settlement by one business day beyond a participant's insolvency.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces an amendment to mitigate this risk by extending insolvency protection of the key elements in a payment cycle – transfer orders, netting and settlement – by one business day beyond the day on which a participant becomes insolvent.

sections.label: MAS designation of FAST and NETS
sections.summary: MAS intends to designate FAST and the NETS EFTPOS debit card system in 2018 as they meet designation criteria.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: MAS intends to designate FAST and Network for Electronic Transfers (NETS) Electronic Funds Transfer at Point-Of-Sale (EFTPOS) debit card system in 2018, as they meet the criteria for designation.

sections.label: Penalty for offence
sections.summary: The penalty is a maximum fine of $100,000, imprisonment of up to two years, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The penalty will be a maximum fine of $100,000, or imprisonment for a term of up to two years, or both.

sections.label: MAS approval for DS rules
sections.summary: The Bill requires a DS to seek MAS approval before rules on its essential roles, responsibilities and operations are implemented or amended.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Bill will also introduce a requirement for a DS to seek approval from MAS before rules which govern the essential roles, responsibilities and operations of a DS can be implemented or amended.

sections.label: Key officers face consequences
sections.summary: Key officers, including senior executives, who fail to take reasonable care or play a key part in an offence will face consequences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Should key officers, including senior executives, fail to take reasonable care or play a key part in the commission of offence, they will have to face the consequences.

sections.label: Protection of transfer orders and netting
sections.summary: The amendments protect transfer orders, netting and settlement, extended one business day beyond insolvency day, giving certainty and finality to DS transactions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The new amendments offer protection of transfer orders, netting and settlement and is extended by one business day beyond insolvency day, providing certainty and finality to DS transactions.

sections.label: Contingencies for bank insolvencies
sections.summary: The question asks what contingencies exist for insolvencies of a foreign bank or domestic operators such as BCS affected by other operational risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: What are the contingencies made in the case of insolvencies of a foreign bank in this instance or, for that matter, domestic operators, such as BCS, should they be affected by other operational risks?

sections.label: Article 3(1) enforceability rule
sections.summary: Article 3(1) makes transfer orders and netting legally enforceable in insolvency proceedings and binding on third parties if entered before insolvency proceedings open.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The main rule in Article 3(1) is that transfer orders and netting shall be legally enforceable, even in the event of insolvency proceedings against a participant and shall be binding on third parties provided that transfer orders were entered into the system before the moment of opening of insolvency proceedings.

sections.label: Bill timing issue versus EU directive
sections.summary: MAS says the amendments are consistent with EU law, but the Bill does not address Article 3(1) timing, while clause 12 allows netting up to one business day after.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: MAS Consultation Paper also states in paragraph 2.2 that the proposed amendments are consistent with the laws of the EU.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, neither does the Bill expressly address the timing issue stated in Article 3(1) of the EU directive on whether such transactions have to be entered into before the commencement of the insolvency event, nor address what happens if transactions are entered into the system after the commencement of an insolvency event, regardless of whether a DS has actual or constructive knowledge of the commencement of the insolvency event.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In fact, clause 12 of the Bill, which amends section 12 of FNA, makes it clear that the DS operator may effect netting of all obligations owed to or by the participant up to and including one business day after.

sections.label: Protection after insolvency with one-day window
sections.summary: Transfer orders entered after insolvency are protected if a central counter-party or clearing house shows no awareness, with a one business day window instead of the EU Directive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: It protects transfer orders that are entered into the system after the moment of insolvency provided that a central counter-party or clearing house demonstrates that they were not aware, nor should have been aware of the commencement of insolvency proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We have chosen not to emulate the EU Directive, but instead provide for a window – one business day – for transactions to be protected even after insolvency is declared.

sections.label: Multi-jurisdiction settlement time zones
sections.summary: A system spanning multiple jurisdictions and time zones, like CLS, may need more than one day to settle in a distress situation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: First, a system that spans multiple jurisdictions across numerous time zones, such as the CLS system which needs more than one day to settle transactions in a distress situation as the distressed participant may face difficulty paying its obligations, usually in multiple currencies.

sections.label: Safeguards against protection abuse
sections.summary: Safeguards exist: designated systems are expected to have rules to exclude insolvent participants and stem fund outflows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Notwithstanding, there are safeguards to prevent abuse of this protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We expect DSs to have rules in place to exclude an insolvent system participant from the DS as soon as it is aware of the insolvency and to stem any outflow of funds which abuse the protection.

sections.label: MAS supervision of BCS and Citi
sections.summary: MAS tracks the financial health of BCS and Citi and has resolution tools at its disposal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As part of ongoing supervision, MAS tracks the financial health of BCS and Citi as well and has resolution tools at our disposal.
